d.s: Sika ViscoCrete-20 HE is a third generation superplasticiser designed for the production of concrete with high early strength characteristics. The special formulation of Sika ViscoCrete-20 HE optimises the dispersion of the binder and at the same time improves the concrete consistency and cohesion.
a: Promote high density and impermeable concrete through extreme high water reduction.
Pronounced increase in the early strength development and set times.
Increases the durability of the concrete.
Improved flowability, placing and compacting behaviour,suitable for the production of self compacting concrete.
Suitable for use in reinforced and pre-stressed concrete.
us: Production of concrete mixes which require high early strength development, powerful water reduction and improved flowability.
In situ concrete requiring fast stripping time
d.pk: Bulk supply, 1000 litre IBC, 205 litre drum, 10 litre container.

sec.t: Sika ViscoCrete-20 HE meets and exceeds all requirements of Australian Standard 1478.1-2000 for High Range Water Reducer Type (HWR).
Stored at temperature between 5ºC and 35ºC in unopened original containers protected from direct sunlight and frost, shelf life is one (1) year.
Sika ViscoCrete-20 HE must be stored in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +35 °C, protected from direct sunlight.

Sika ViscoCrete-20 HE is added to the initial batching water. For optimum utilisation of the high water reduction we recommend thorough mixing at a minimal wet mixing time of 60 seconds per cubic meter. The addition of the remaining gauging water, to fine tune concrete consistency, should only be started after 2/3 of the wet mixing time, to avoid surplus water in the concrete.

Sika ViscoCrete-20 HE may be combined with many other Sika Concrete Admixtures, except Sikament NN. Trials must always be carried out before combining products in specific mixes. Contact Sika Technical Services for additional information and any specific combinations.
Dosage is 200 ml to 1000 ml per 100kg of total cementitious material. Optimum dosage should be determined by site trials.
